dedupe_keys.name: water and planetary health analytics wapha global metal mines database

description: The WAPHA global metal mines database is a geo-referenced inventory of known metal mining sites and of intact and failed tailings storage facilities worldwide, built by Mark Macklin, Karen Hudson-Edwards, John Owen, Deanna Kemp, Paolo Scussolini, Alex Lechner and colleagues to assess how toxic mining waste (lead, zinc, copper and arsenic) contaminates rivers and floodplains. With process-based and empirically tested models, the authors estimated that metal mines affect 479,200 km of river channels and 164,000 square kilometres of floodplains, and that about 23 million people live on contaminated floodplains, almost fifty times more than are directly affected by tailings dam failures. The deposit, dated 7 September 2023 with DOI 10.5061/dryad.j3tx95xmg, holds spreadsheets of active and inactive mines (as of 17 May 2023), zipped shapefiles of tailings storage and tailings dam failure sites, a README and the model code, released free under CC0. Caveats: locations and status come from heterogeneous public sources, and the contamination estimates are model outputs, not measurements. For simulation it supports hazard exposure and environmental impact studies of mining on rivers, water supply and agriculture downstream. Related catalogue records include the Global Tailings Portal and the WISE Uranium chronology of tailings dam failures.
